transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ChatGPT. What brings you in today?

Hi. Well, my supervisor basically made me come in. It’s because I keep leaving my station on the production line. Which, by the way, I work at this plastics factory and the smell is just... ugh, it gets right into your clothes and your hair. I had to buy this special shampoo from Target just to get the chemical smell out, and it was like twelve dollars for a tiny bottle, which is a total rip-off if you ask me. 

But yeah, I guess I also keep popping up during our shift meetings when we're supposed to just stay put and listen to the daily quotas. Those metal folding chairs they have us sit on are literally the worst, they pinch the back of your legs if you're wearing shorts. But my boss says my walking away is becoming a huge safety problem on the floor. I don't even mean to do it, I just... take off before I even think about it. Like my feet just start moving. The other day I was just walking over to tell my coworker Dave about this crazy car accident I saw on the highway on my way in—this red Honda was totally smashed into the median—and then my boss started yelling at me about safety hazards and leaving my machine running. So, yeah, that's why I'm here.
When you leave your station or get up during meetings, is it usually because you feel restless or distracted, or because you’re intentionally ignoring the rules?

Oh, no, I'm definitely not trying to be bad or ignore the rules! My boss probably thinks I am, but it's really not like that. It's just... when I try to stand still by my machine for too long, or when we have to sit through those safety trainings... which, by the way, the guy in the safety video they make us watch is wearing the most ridiculous goggles. They look straight out of the 1980s. I told Dave they probably bought a VHS tape at a garage sale and just put it on the computer. 

But yeah, when I'm just standing or sitting there, it feels like this... this intense pressure is just building up inside my body. And I literally just have to move. Like I have to pace around, or stretch, or just go do something right that second. If I don't, I feel like I'm gonna pop. Speaking of popping, they had this air valve blow on the line next to mine last month and it sounded like a literal bomb went off. My ears were ringing for like two days straight. I thought I was going deaf! So I was looking up if you can get workers' comp for hearing loss, and there's this whole complicated website for it... but yeah, I don't mean to break the rules, I just have to get up and move, you know?
When you get up or leave your station, is it usually because you feel distracted by something else and lose track of what you were doing?

Well, I guess... yeah, I definitely get distracted. It's like, I'm working on the line, right? And I'll hear one beep from another machine, or somebody walks past with a pallet jack... which, oh my gosh, the wheels on those things are so squeaky. They sound like dying mice. I told maintenance they need to grease them, and the guy just looked at me like I was crazy. He was eating a tuna sandwich at the time, and I could smell it from like five feet away. I hate tuna. My mom used to make tuna casserole every Friday when I was growing up, with those crushed-up potato chips on top? Disgusting. 

But anyway, yeah, someone walks by with the pallet jack, and it just pulls my eyes and my whole brain completely away from what I'm doing. Even though I totally know I'm supposed to stay at my own station. It's just like my brain has to know what that noise is, or where that person is going. Did you know Dave actually ran over his own foot with a pallet jack once? He had to wear this big gray boot for like six weeks. It looked so heavy, I don't know how he walked around in it. But yeah, I just lose track of everything else.
Were you having similar problems with distractibility or leaving your seat when you were a child?

Yeah, oh totally. Even back in elementary school, I was always that kid. Like, I literally could not stay in my seat to save my life. I was always talking over the teacher, too. Mrs. Gable, my third-grade teacher, she used to wear these giant chunky necklaces made of, like, painted wooden blocks? They were so loud every time she moved. She was always sending notes home to my mom because I kept blurting things out or just getting up and wandering around the room to look at the class pet. We had a guinea pig named Barnaby. He smelled terrible, kind of like cedar shavings and old pee. I actually tried to feed him a piece of my fruit roll-up once, which was a terrible idea because it got stuck to his little teeth. The school nurse had to come help get it off, and she smelled like rubbing alcohol and peppermint. But yeah, my mom had this whole stack of notes from the school just sitting on top of the microwave for years. So, yeah, it's definitely been happening since I was little.
